name: Proxmox_VE_Cluster_Topology
description: Cluster, node and guest topology for Proxmox VE: cluster to node, node to guest.
technicalNotes:
One per cluster is enough, since it reports the whole cluster from wherever it runs. It works with addERI_Proxmox_VE_Node, which stamps the node keys on every node's resource, with Proxmox_VE_Cluster_GuestStatus's instance ERIs, which draw a guest that is not a resource of its own, and with Proxmox_VE_Cluster_Status's, which draw the cluster.

Emits two kinds of edge. Cluster to node, type "Cluster" -- only on a cluster; a standalone host gets no cluster vertex and no Cluster edges. Node to guest, type "Compute", the edge that matters: it lets a node's alerts explain the alerts of its guests.

Guests are matched to their own LogicMonitor resources by MAC address, read from the guest config (net0 and friends). LogicMonitor already keys a monitored resource on its MACs, so the two meet with no name matching -- a guest called "Kiosk01" whose resource is "Kiosk01 - Display" still connects. It is the identity VMware_vSphere_VirtualMachine_Topology uses. A guest with no readable MAC falls back to a synthesised key, as the VMware module does.

A vertex is drawn only if it matches a resource or a DataSource instance carrying predef.externalResourceID. A guest that is its own resource matches once LogicMonitor's discovery has put its MAC in that resource's predef.externalResourceID, over SNMP or WMI. Every other guest is drawn through Proxmox_VE_Cluster_GuestStatus, whose discovery puts the same key on the guest's instance.

Proxmox exposes no hardware UUID or MAC for a node, so each node vertex carries one synthesised key, proxmoxve--node--<node>--<ip> with the address /cluster/status reports for that node, and addERI_Proxmox_VE_Node stamps the same key on each node's own resource from its system.ips. It needs no cluster name, so a node without the token matches with no property set, and one group can hold the nodes of every cluster. Only a node /cluster/status gives no address falls back to proxmoxve--<cluster>--<node>. Never both: the portal matches a multi-key vertex only to a resource carrying every key. A node whose resource lacks the key is not drawn.

The cluster vertex, keyed proxmoxve--<cluster>, is drawn through Proxmox_VE_Cluster_Status's one instance, which carries that key as type Cluster; an instance vertex takes edges from every matched node.

Limitation: not yet tested with the nodes of two clusters in one portal. The node key is the node's name plus its address, so two clusters whose nodes share both would be joined on the map.

Cost: one /cluster/status, one /cluster/resources per type, and one config read per guest. That last is O(guests), acceptable because this runs hourly, on one resource per cluster, and the MAC is available nowhere else.

Like the two addERI modules, this cannot be compiled or run outside a Collector: it works through com.logicmonitor.mod.Snippets (eriPreProcessor, isMac, generateTopology), whose output format LogicMonitor does not fully document.

Applies on the cluster role: resources whose pve.cluster.role is active or standby, which the NetScan sets. Only one of the pair collects -- the active resource, or the standby while the active one is down or has lost quorum. The other prints nothing, so its datapoints read No Data and the pair never alerts twice. The suite has no addCategory_* PropertySource: the NetScan sets the categories and pve.cluster.role, and the product page lists them for a resource added by hand.

Requires Sys.Audit on / for /cluster/status and VM.Audit on /vms/{vmid} for the guest list and configs; the PVEAuditor role includes both. A guest the token cannot see is not drawn.
